name: The full ledger
note: Every good and recipe of the 21 September 2026 brainstorm. A map to cut from, not a scope. Icons and signs are 16 px concept placeholders generated in chat: pre-production material.

tagNamespaces.note: Production stage: raw, processed, compound, magistery, assembly, finished.
For raw goods: mined, quarried, farmed, herded or magical.
The shelf the good sits on in the ledger.
Which population Need buys it: food, intoxicants-and-physic, clothing, wares, works-and-arms.
mundane, alchemical (mineral chemistry) or magical (Essence somewhere upstream).
What sort of stuff it is: metal, acid, pigment, fibre and so on.
Gameplay-relevant properties: toxic, corrosive, explosive, perishable, luxury, staple, by-product, hub.
Association with one of your named archetypes. Only Lakefolk, Jadefolk and Steelfolk are used; other cultures get an origin tag instead.
Earth region the good is historically tied to, for mapping onto archetypes later.

tags.note: Fits the heart slot of a golem.

goods.name: Native copper
goods.note: The one metal you can find already metal, green with verdigris where the air has touched it.

goods.name: Ironstone
goods.note: Red, heavy and everywhere. The cheapest ore and the hungriest for fuel.

goods.name: Cassiterite
goods.note: Dark, heavy crystals. Rare in the world, which is why bronze made empires trade.

goods.name: Galena
goods.note: Usually carries a little silver.

goods.name: Calamine
goods.note: Looks like nothing. Its metal boils away in the furnace, so for centuries it was known only through brass.

goods.name: Native silver
goods.note: Grows in wires and ferns inside the rock. Tarnishes black, polishes white.

goods.name: Gold nuggets
goods.note: Never rusts, never hides. The only ore a child can identify.

goods.name: Cinnabar
goods.note: Heavy vermilion stone. Heat it and the red turns to running silver.

goods.name: Rock salt
goods.note: Mined in blocks, grey or pink. The same stuff as the sea, a few million years drier.

goods.name: Native sulfur
goods.note: Yellow crystals at volcanic vents. Burns blue and stinks of the underworld.

goods.name: Blue vitriol crystals
goods.note: Blue crystals that grow where copper mines weep. Iron dipped in the solution comes out copper-coated, which looked like transmutation.

goods.name: Nitre earth
goods.note: Dug from caves, or farmed in a nitre bed.

goods.name: Realgar
goods.note: Red arsenic ore, with yellow orpiment.

goods.name: Stibnite
goods.note: Bundles of grey metallic blades. Ground fine, it has lined eyes as kohl for four thousand years.

goods.name: Bismuth ore
goods.note: A pink-tinged silver metal, long mistaken for tin or lead. The least poisonous of the heavy metals.

goods.name: Alum stone
goods.note: A pale rock, worthless until roasted and leached. Popes and sultans fought over good deposits.

goods.name: Sal ammoniac crust
goods.note: Volcanic vents and burning coal seams.

goods.name: Limestone
goods.note: Old seabed. Burn it and it becomes the most useful white powder in the tree.

goods.name: Cobalt ore
goods.note: The kobold ore, with pink cobalt bloom.

goods.name: Tincal
goods.note: Raw borax from dry lake beds.

goods.name: Natron
goods.note: A crust from dry salt lakes. Egypt embalmed its dead in it and made glass with it.

goods.name: Coal
goods.note: Fuel and reducer. Hotter than wood, dirtier than charcoal.

goods.name: Marcasite
goods.note: Fool's gold. Weathers into green vitriol.

goods.name: Lodestone
goods.note: A natural magnet. The stone that made open-ocean navigation possible.

goods.name: Magnesia nigra
goods.note: Pyrolusite, the glassmaker's soap: it takes the green out of glass.

goods.name: Soil, any of 17
goods.note: The terrain generator's surfaces, dug as a resource.

goods.name: Kaolin
goods.note: China clay.

goods.name: Gypsum
goods.note: Soft enough to scratch with a fingernail. Heat it gently and it becomes plaster.

goods.name: Bitumen
goods.note: Rock tar that seeps from the ground. Waterproofs anything and burns fiercely.

goods.name: Lapis lazuli
goods.note: Deep blue stone flecked with fool's gold. For centuries it came from a single valley.

goods.name: Jade
goods.note: Tougher than steel to carve, cool to the touch. Some peoples value it above gold.

goods.name: Amber
goods.note: Fossil resin, warm and light. Rub it and it attracts dust: the first electricity anyone noticed.

sign.reading: stone or gem + resin or gum

goods.name: Obsidian
goods.note: Volcanic glass. Flakes to an edge sharper than any steel, and shatters as easily.

goods.name: Rock crystal
goods.note: Clear quartz. The ancients thought it was ice frozen too hard to melt.

goods.name: Grain
goods.note: Wheat, barley or rye, as the climate allows. Bread and beer both start here.

goods.name: Rice
goods.note: The wet-field staple. Feeds more people per field than anything else, if you have the water.

goods.name: Maize
goods.note: Huge yields, one catch: it must be cooked with lime or the people who live on it fall ill.

goods.name: Grapes
goods.note: Looks like a luxury crop. Turns out to feed half the chemistry in this tree.

sign.reading: fruit or nut + cup or vessel

goods.name: Olives
goods.note: Slow trees, long lives. Oil for food, lamps and the best soap.

goods.name: Flax
goods.note: Fibre and oil seed from one plant.

goods.name: Hemp
goods.note: Coarse, strong and rot-resistant. The ship's crop: rope and sailcloth.

goods.name: Cotton
goods.note: Soft fibre from a warm-country boll. Light, washable, cool to wear.

goods.name: Sugar cane
goods.note: A giant grass that stores sugar. Hungry for heat, water and labour.

sign.reading: grain or grass + bee: honey and wax

goods.name: Tea leaves
goods.note: Leaves of an evergreen bush. Worth an ocean voyage once people acquire the habit.

goods.name: Cacao
goods.note: Pods from a rainforest tree. Bitter, stimulating, and once used as money.

goods.name: Coffee cherries
goods.note: Red cherries with a bitter seed. The drink of people who want to stay awake and argue.

goods.name: Opium poppy
goods.note: Score the green pod and it bleeds the most effective painkiller of the age.

goods.name: Agave
goods.note: A desert rosette that takes a decade to mature. Its sap ferments in days.

goods.name: Madder root
goods.note: A scrambling weed with red roots. The colour of soldiers' coats and Turkey carpets.

goods.name: Indigo plant
goods.note: A shrub whose green leaves hide the deepest blue. Getting it out is a foul business.

goods.name: Weld
goods.note: A roadside weed that gives the clearest, fastest yellow.

goods.name: Timber
goods.note: The universal input: fuel, ash, planks, charcoal. Forests set the ceiling on everything.

goods.name: Oak galls
goods.note: Lumps a wasp makes an oak grow. Packed with the tannin that turns iron salts black.

sign.reading: fruit or nut + tree or wood

goods.name: Tanbark
goods.note: Oak bark, stripped and ground. A hide soaks in it for a year to become leather.

goods.name: Pine resin
goods.note: Tapped from living pines. Distil it for turpentine, boil it down for pitch.

sign.reading: resin or gum + tree or wood

goods.name: Herbs and hops
goods.note: The physic garden and the brewer's bittering, in one basket.

goods.name: Spices
goods.note: Light, dry, imperishable and wildly overpriced. The ideal long-distance cargo.

goods.name: Kelp
goods.note: Seaweed burnt on the beach for its ash. A coast's answer to natron.

goods.name: Lacquer sap
goods.note: Milky sap of the lacquer tree. Raises blisters raw, cures harder than any varnish.

goods.name: Mulberry leaves
goods.note: The only thing silkworms will eat. No mulberry, no silk.

goods.name: Gum arabic
goods.note: Hardened tears of the acacia. The binder in ink, watercolour and sweets.

goods.name: Dammar resin
goods.note: Clear resin tapped from rainforest trees. The painter's favourite varnish, and torch fuel where it grows.

goods.name: Camphor
goods.note: White crystals distilled from the wood of a giant tree. Cool, piercing, and worth more than gold at the right port.

goods.name: Benzoin
goods.note: A sweet, vanilla-smelling gum cut from forest trees. The base note of half the world's incense.

goods.name: Frankincense and myrrh
goods.note: Tears of thorny desert trees. Temples burn them by the ton, so whoever holds the groves holds a steady income.

goods.name: Bamboo
goods.note: A grass that thinks it is timber. Grows a foot a day; pulps into paper.

sign.reading: grain or grass + tree or wood

goods.name: Coconut
goods.note: Food, drink, oil and, from the husk, a rope that salt water cannot rot.

sign.reading: fruit or nut + thread or fibre

goods.name: Areca nut
goods.note: The seed at the heart of the betel quid. Mild, habit-forming, and chewed by a tenth of the world.

goods.name: Dyewood
goods.note: Sappan in the east, brazilwood in the west, camwood in the south: heartwoods that bleed red. One of them named a country.

goods.name: Palm oil
goods.note: Red oil pressed from palm fruit. Food at home; abroad it becomes soap, candles and the flux for tinplate.

goods.name: Kola nut
goods.note: Bitter, stimulating, and the proper gift for a host. Travels weeks wrapped in wet leaves.

goods.name: Cutch
goods.note: Dark extract boiled from acacia heartwood. Tans leather, dyes cloth khaki, and goes into the betel quid.

goods.name: Wool
goods.note: Sheared yearly, so the sheep is a renewable mine. Takes dye better than any plant fibre.

goods.name: Hides
goods.note: A by-product of meat. Rots in days unless salted, limed or tanned.

goods.name: Tallow
goods.note: Rendered beef and mutton fat. Poor people's light and everyone's soap.

goods.name: Bone
goods.note: Slaughterhouse leftovers. Boil for glue, burn for the ash that refines silver.

goods.name: Horn
goods.note: Translucent when pressed thin: lantern panes, combs, spectacle frames.

goods.name: Milk
goods.note: Spoils by evening. Everything done with it is a way of making it keep.

goods.name: Dung
goods.note: A gentle, steady heat as it rots, and the base of a nitre bed.

goods.name: Urine
goods.note: The alchemists' most underrated raw material.

goods.name: Ox blood
goods.note: Caught at the slaughterhouse. Clarifies sugar and wine, and once, by accident, made a new blue.

goods.name: Honeycomb
goods.note: Two goods in one: honey to eat, wax to burn and seal.

goods.name: Cochineal
goods.note: Scale insects farmed on cactus pads.

goods.name: Eggs
goods.note: Food first. The white also clears wine and sticks down gold leaf; the yolk binds paint.

goods.name: Quills
goods.note: Goose flight feathers, from the left wing for right-handed writers.

goods.name: Fish
goods.note: Cheap protein that spoils in a day. Salt turns it into a trade good.

goods.name: Furs
goods.note: Beaver above all: its barbed underfur felts better than any other.

goods.name: Silk cocoons
goods.note: Silkworms eat nothing else.

goods.name: Sticklac
goods.note: Resin crust that scale insects leave on twigs. One harvest gives a varnish, a wax and a red dye.

goods.name: Shells
goods.note: Burn them and you have lime without a quarry. Small glossy ones have also passed as money across half the world.

goods.name: Essence
goods.note: Your magical fuel. Every magistery and both great assemblies draw on it.

goods.name: Copper
goods.note: Red, soft, and the best carrier of heat. Half of it ends up in alloys.

goods.name: Iron
goods.note: Wrought in a bloomery or cast from a blast furnace. Either way it eats forests or coal.

goods.name: Tin
goods.note: Soft and bright, and it cries when bent. Almost never used alone.

goods.name: Lead
goods.note: Heavy, soft, melts on a kitchen fire. Roofs, pipes, shot and slow poison.

goods.name: Spelter
goods.note: The bluish metal caught by condensing calamine's fumes. Spelter was its trade name.

goods.name: Silver
goods.note: Also cupelled out of galena lead on a bed of bone ash.

goods.name: Gold
goods.note: Pure, heavy and useless for tools. Its whole value is that it stays.

goods.name: Quicksilver
goods.note: Roast cinnabar, condense the vapour.

goods.name: Salt
goods.note: Preserves meat, fish, hides and cheese. A settlement without salt cannot store food.

goods.name: Brimstone
goods.note: Sulfur melted and cast into sticks. Gunpowder, bleaching and fumigation.

goods.name: Oil of vitriol
goods.note: The first strong acid. Parent of the others.

goods.name: Nitre
goods.note: Nitre liquor was really treated with wood ash.

goods.name: White arsenic
goods.note: A white powder sublimed from roasting arsenic ore. Tasteless, which made it the poisoner's favourite.

goods.name: Star regulus
goods.note: Stibnite was really reduced with iron to get the star.

goods.name: Bismuth crystal
goods.note: Melt bismuth, let it cool slowly, and it builds itself into rainbow staircases.

goods.name: Pearl ash
goods.note: Wood ash leached, boiled dry in an iron pot, then baked white. The original potash.

goods.name: Alum
goods.note: The mordant that makes dye bite into cloth. Also tans white leather, sizes paper and slows fire.

goods.name: Sal ammoniac
goods.note: Egypt made it from the soot of burnt dung.

goods.name: Quicklime
goods.note: Burnt limestone. Add water and it boils. Strips hides, makes mortar, sharpens lye and unlocks maize.

goods.name: Zaffre
goods.note: Roasted cobalt ore, a blue-making powder.

goods.name: Borax
goods.note: Flux for brazing and enamel.

goods.name: Soda ash
goods.note: Or burn kelp for it.

goods.name: Wood ash
goods.note: What is left of a tree. Ten tons of wood give about a bucket of potash.

goods.name: Green vitriol
goods.note: Iron vitriol: for ink, black dye and Prussian blue.

goods.name: Plaster
goods.note: Gypsum baked and ground. Add water and it sets in minutes.

goods.name: Potter's clay
goods.note: From Limosol and Fluvisol.

goods.name: Sand
goods.note: From Arenosol.

goods.name: Ochre
goods.note: From Rubrisol and Vertisol.

goods.name: Fuller's earth
goods.note: From Cinerisol, the bleachearth. Scours grease out of wool.

goods.name: Peat
goods.note: From Turbisol. A poor Domain's coal.

goods.name: Nitre bed
goods.note: Farmed saltpetre: a year of rotting, then leach.

goods.name: Flour
goods.note: Ground grain. Keeps for months, where bread keeps for days.

goods.name: Malt
goods.note: Grain tricked into sprouting, then dried. The sprouting makes the sugar that beer needs.

goods.name: Wine
goods.note: Grape juice left alone. Parent of vinegar, brandy and tartar.

goods.name: Olive oil
goods.note: Pressed, not cooked. Food, lamp fuel, and the base of fine soap.

goods.name: Linen thread
goods.note: Flax rotted, beaten, combed and spun. Laborious, which is why linen was never cheap.

goods.name: Linseed oil
goods.note: The drying oil behind paint, varnish and printer's ink.

goods.name: Hemp fibre
goods.note: Longer and coarser than flax. Hard on the hands, kind to a ship.

sign.reading: thread or fibre + cut or worked

goods.name: Cotton thread
goods.note: Short fibres, so it needs a good spinner. The thread of the everyday.

goods.name: Sugar
goods.note: Boiled down from cane juice and clarified with lime and blood. A spice that became a staple.

goods.name: Opium
goods.note: Dried poppy latex. Medicine in one dose, habit in the next.

goods.name: Pulque
goods.note: Milky, sour and mildly alcoholic. Must be drunk within days, so it never travels.

goods.name: Planks
goods.note: Sawn and seasoned timber. A sawmill turns a forest into a building material.

sign.reading: tree or wood + cut or worked

goods.name: Charcoal
goods.note: Wood baked without air. Burns hotter and cleaner than wood; it is what gunpowder and steel really want.

goods.name: Pitch
goods.note: Resin or tar boiled thick. The black stuff that keeps the sea out of a hull.

goods.name: Turpentine
goods.note: The thin, sharp spirit distilled off pine resin. Thins paint and varnish.

goods.name: Lampblack
goods.note: Soot, collected on purpose.

goods.name: Silk thread
goods.note: One cocoon unwinds into about a kilometre of filament, reeled in hot water several strands at once.

goods.name: Woollen yarn
goods.note: Carded and spun fleece. Every cottage can make it, which is what made wool a national industry.

goods.name: Honey
goods.note: The only sweetener most peoples had. Never spoils.

goods.name: Beeswax
goods.note: Clean-burning, sweet-smelling, expensive. Also the model-maker's material for lost-wax casting.

goods.name: Glue
goods.note: Hides and bones boiled to jelly. Holds furniture, books and paper size together.

goods.name: Bone ash
goods.note: Makes cupels for refining silver, and bone china.

goods.name: Parchment
goods.note: Limed, scraped, stretched skin. Outlasts paper by a thousand years and costs a flock per book.

goods.name: Leather
goods.note: Lime to strip the hair, bark to tan.

goods.name: Cheese
goods.note: Milk made to keep. Salt is what makes the rind.

goods.name: Salt fish
goods.note: Split, salted and dried until it stacks like planks. Fast days and long voyages run on it.

goods.name: Tea
goods.note: Withered, rolled and fired leaf. Light, costly and habit-forming: a perfect Fashion good.

goods.name: Coffee
goods.note: Roasted, ground and boiled. Where it arrives, coffee houses and newspapers follow.

goods.name: Shellac
goods.note: Sticklac washed and melted into amber flakes. The real body of sealing wax and the finest polish for wood.

goods.name: Bronze
goods.note: Copper made hard with tin. Casts beautifully: bells, cannon, statues, bearings.

goods.name: Brass
goods.note: The clockwork metal.

goods.name: Pewter
goods.note: Sold as is: tableware for the middle classes.

goods.name: Type metal
goods.note: Antimony makes it expand as it sets, so letters cast sharp.

goods.name: Steel
goods.note: Iron with just enough carbon. Takes an edge and holds a spring.

goods.name: Tinplate
goods.note: Iron sheet dipped in tin, with sal ammoniac as the flux that makes tin wet iron. Sold as tinware: light, bright, rustproof.

goods.name: Speculum metal
goods.note: High-tin bronze whitened with arsenic: a metal mirror.

goods.name: Gold amalgam
goods.note: Paint it on, burn the mercury off: fire-gilding.

goods.name: Litharge
goods.note: Lead calx from the cupel.

goods.name: Lead shot
goods.note: Arsenic makes the drops fall round.

goods.name: Gold thread
goods.note: Gilt strip wound round a silk core. Cloth of gold is woven from this.

goods.name: Aqua fortis
goods.note: Dissolves silver, not gold. Parts the two. Etches metal.

goods.name: Aqua regia
goods.note: The only water that dissolves gold.

goods.name: Caustic lye
goods.note: Potash sharpened with lime. Dissolves fat and skin alike.

goods.name: Spirit of salt
goods.note: Salt distilled with oil of vitriol. Fumes in air and eats most metals. A second road to aqua regia.

goods.name: Vinegar
goods.note: Wine gone sour on purpose. The weakest acid and the most used.

goods.name: Aqua vitae
goods.note: Brandy, the water of life.

goods.name: Spirit of wine
goods.note: The solvent behind tinctures, varnish and perfume.

goods.name: Spirit of hartshorn
goods.note: Ammonia, from distilled horn or from sal ammoniac and lime.

goods.name: Tartar
goods.note: Wine-cask crust. Mordant and flux.

goods.name: Gunpowder
goods.note: Six parts nitre, one sulfur, one charcoal. The nitre is always the hard part.

goods.name: Vermilion
goods.note: Alchemists rebuilt cinnabar from its parts to get a purer red.

goods.name: Smalt
goods.note: Cobalt-blue glass, ground for pigment or cast for lenses.

goods.name: White lead
goods.note: Lead coils over vinegar, buried in dung for the heat.

goods.name: Red lead
goods.note: Litharge roasted again until it turns orange. Paint for ironwork, flux for glass.

goods.name: Verdigris
goods.note: The green crust copper grows over vinegar. A pigment, and the green in fireworks.

goods.name: Prussian blue
goods.note: Found by accident, from blood.

goods.name: Ultramarine
goods.note: Kneaded out of lapis in a dough of wax and resin.

goods.name: King's yellow
goods.note: Orpiment. Beautiful and poisonous.

goods.name: Jeweller's rouge
goods.note: Calcined green vitriol: the caput mortuum that polishes glass.

goods.name: Madder lake
goods.note: Madder dye fixed onto alum to make a lasting red.

goods.name: Indigo dye
goods.note: The vat ferments in stale urine.

goods.name: Weld yellow
goods.note: Weld on an alum mordant. Over indigo it makes the only good green.

goods.name: Scarlet dye
goods.note: Cochineal on a tin mordant: the brightest red of the age.

goods.name: Iron black
goods.note: Oak galls and green vitriol: the same chemistry as ink, in a dye vat.

goods.name: Pigments
goods.note: The colourman's stock. Every hue has a different mine, plant or poison behind it.

goods.name: Glass
goods.note: Sand, soda and lime, melted. Greenish unless you correct it.

goods.name: Lead crystal
goods.note: Glass made heavy and brilliant with lead. Rings when struck, sparkles when cut.

goods.name: Window glass
goods.note: Panes set in lead cames.

goods.name: Lenses
goods.note: Ground against sand, polished with rouge. Weeks of work in each good one.

goods.name: Enamel
goods.note: Coloured glass powder fused onto metal. Colour that cannot fade.

goods.name: Glaze
goods.note: A glassy skin fired onto clay. Lead makes it flow; cobalt makes it blue.

goods.name: Paper
goods.note: Rag paper, sized with alum and glue.

sign.reading: page or book + thread or fibre

goods.name: Iron-gall ink
goods.note: Pale when written, black by morning. Eats through the page in a few centuries.

goods.name: Printer's ink
goods.note: Lampblack in boiled linseed oil. Sticky enough to cling to metal type.

goods.name: Oil paints
goods.note: Pigment ground into linseed oil. Dries slowly, which lets a painter blend.

goods.name: Varnish
goods.note: Resin dissolved in oil and turpentine. The glow on a violin.

goods.name: Lacquer
goods.note: Dozens of thin coats, each cured in damp air. Vermilion makes the classic red.

goods.name: Sealing wax
goods.note: Snap, melt, press. Vermilion for letters, black for mourning.

sign.reading: bee: honey and wax + page or book

goods.name: Candles
goods.note: Tallow for the kitchen, beeswax for the altar and the ballroom.

goods.name: Soap
goods.note: Fat boiled with lye. Olive oil makes it hard and white; tallow makes it cheap.

goods.name: Rope
goods.note: Hemp yarn twisted in a ropewalk a quarter of a mile long, then tarred.

goods.name: Canvas
goods.note: Hemp woven tight. Sails, tents, sacks and painters' grounds.

goods.name: Linen
goods.note: Cool, strong, and whiter with every wash. Underclothes, sheets, and in the end rags for paper.

goods.name: Woollen cloth
goods.note: Fulled: pounded in fuller's earth and stale urine.

goods.name: Cotton cloth
goods.note: Light and washable. Printed and dyed, it is the cloth that launches fashions.

goods.name: Silk
goods.note: Strong, light, lustrous. The cloth that named a trade route.

goods.name: Mortar
goods.note: Slaked lime and sand. Sets slowly by drinking the air.

goods.name: Bricks
goods.note: Clay shaped and fired. A city that burns down once rebuilds in brick.

goods.name: Pottery
goods.note: Thrown, glazed and fired. Every household owns some, so the volume is enormous.

goods.name: Porcelain
goods.note: The white gold. Europe's recipe was cracked by an alchemist held prisoner to make the yellow kind.

goods.name: Bread
goods.note: The staple. Its price is the first thing a population riots about.

goods.name: Beer
goods.note: Malt and water, bittered with hops so it keeps. Safer than the well.

sign.reading: cup or vessel + grain or grass

goods.name: Nixtamal
goods.note: Lime unlocks the maize. Without it a maize people sickens.

goods.name: Rice wine
goods.note: Rice brewed with a mould starter. Served warm.

goods.name: Mead
goods.note: Honey and water, fermented. Possibly the oldest drink there is.

sign.reading: cup or vessel + bee: honey and wax

goods.name: Chocolate
goods.note: Cacao ground with sugar and spice, whisked to a froth. Drunk, not eaten.

sign.reading: cup or vessel + fruit or nut

goods.name: Potable gold
goods.note: Gold dissolved in aqua regia and tamed until it can be swallowed. The basis of every elixir.

goods.name: Thundergold
goods.note: Fulminating gold: a real, touchy explosive.

goods.name: Lunar caustic
goods.note: Silver dissolved and recrystallised.

goods.name: Phosphorus
goods.note: Cold fire, first boiled out of urine by a man looking for gold.

goods.name: Ruby glass
goods.note: Gold and tin make the purple that turns glass ruby.

goods.name: Quintessence
goods.note: Essence rectified in spirit of wine.

goods.name: Philosophical mercury
goods.note: Quicksilver sharpened on the star regulus.

goods.name: Philosophers' stone
goods.note: A capstone, perhaps an Aspiration.

goods.name: Quickblood
goods.note: Mercury is the spirit. Potable gold is the upgrade.

goods.name: Golem body
goods.note: Salt is the body principle. The soil decides the function.

goods.name: Arsenic heart
goods.note: Cheap, toxic, short-lived.

goods.name: Antimony heart
goods.note: The dependable standard.

goods.name: Bismuth heart
goods.note: Clean, stable, holds the most instruction.

goods.name: Command plate
goods.note: Brass etched with aqua fortis: the golem's written orders.

goods.name: Clockwork
goods.note: Brass wheels, steel springs. The first machine that runs without being pushed.

goods.name: Golem
goods.note: Needs blood, body, one heart and a plate. Optional: bronze joints, smalt eyes, lunar-caustic nerves, clockwork hands.

goods.name: Hull
goods.note: Copper sheathing under the waterline, or whatever a Domain-ship has instead.

goods.name: Sails
goods.note: Alum makes cloth slow to burn.

goods.name: Rigging
goods.note: Miles of tarred rope per ship. A vessel is as much cordage as timber.

goods.name: Compass
goods.note: A magnetised needle under glass. Lets a ship hold a course with no land or stars in sight.

goods.name: Spyglass
goods.note: Two lenses in a brass tube. See the harbour, or the pirate, an hour sooner.

goods.name: Charts
goods.note: A captain's most valuable and most secret possession.

goods.name: Aether engine
goods.note: Pure invention: the thing that makes an aethership an aethership.

goods.name: Ship's provisions
goods.note: Salt fish, hard bread and beer. How far a ship can go is how much of this it carries.

goods.name: Aethership
goods.note: The thing that reaches the next Domain. Hemp, timber and brass, held aloft by an engine nobody fully understands.

goods.name: Tortillas
goods.note: Nixtamal patted thin and baked on a hot stone. The daily bread of maize country.

goods.name: Laudanum
goods.note: Opium in spirit of wine. Its physician's name meant 'worthy of praise'.

goods.name: Theriac
goods.note: The cure-all of sixty ingredients, cut to four.

goods.name: Antimonial cup
goods.note: Wine left in it overnight becomes a purge. Reusable forever.

goods.name: Mercurial ointment
goods.note: Quicksilver ground into fat. The standard cure for the pox, and nearly as bad.

goods.name: Smelling salts
goods.note: A whiff of ammonia under the nose. Fainting was fashionable; so was the remedy.

goods.name: Tinctures
goods.note: Herbs steeped in spirit of wine. Keeps for years where the fresh plant lasts a week.

goods.name: Elixir
goods.note: Your potion of youth.

goods.name: Betel quid
goods.note: Areca, a smear of lime and a leaf to wrap it. Without the lime it does nothing.

goods.name: Everyday clothes
goods.note: What most people wear most days. Dull, steady, enormous demand.

goods.name: Fast-dyed cloth
goods.note: Alum is the mordant that makes colour stay.

goods.name: Scarlet cloth
goods.note: The brightest cloth money can buy. Cardinals, officers and anyone who wants to be seen.

goods.name: Court dress
goods.note: Silk, scarlet and gold thread. Worn twice, talked about for a season.

goods.name: Felt hats
goods.note: Mercury in aqua fortis mats the fur. It also maddens the hatter.

goods.name: Shoes
goods.note: Everyone needs them and everyone wears them out.

goods.name: Cosmetics
goods.note: Kohl from stibnite, ceruse from white lead, pearl white from bismuth.

goods.name: Batik cloth
goods.note: Draw in hot wax, dye, boil the wax out. The pattern is whatever the wax protected.

goods.name: Looking glass
goods.note: Tin foil and quicksilver behind glass: the real Venetian secret.

goods.name: Scrying mirror
goods.note: A looking glass silvered twice, once for the eye and once for elsewhere. How you see the next Domain before you go.

goods.name: Printed books
goods.note: Cast type, rag paper, oil ink, a leather back. Four trades meet in every volume.

goods.name: Writing set
goods.note: Ink, quills, paper and wax. What a clerk, a merchant or a lover needs.

goods.name: Lucentware
goods.note: My guess at your coinage: crystal that holds a cold light.

goods.name: Cold lamp
goods.note: A sealed glass with a little phosphorus. Glows without flame, heat or smoke.

goods.name: Blue-and-white ware
goods.note: Cobalt painted under a clear glaze. The most copied ceramics in history.

goods.name: Lacquerware
goods.note: Wood under many coats of lacquer. Waterproof, feather-light and glass-smooth.

sign.reading: cup or vessel + resin or gum

goods.name: Jewellery
goods.note: Gold soldered with borax, set with whatever stone the wearer's culture prizes.

goods.name: Silverware
goods.note: Spoons, cups and candlesticks. A family's savings, displayed on the sideboard.

goods.name: Gilded ware
goods.note: Bronze painted with gold amalgam, then heated until the mercury flies off. Splendid, and deadly to the gilder.

goods.name: Enamelware
goods.note: Copper coated in fused coloured glass. Snuffboxes, watch cases, reliquaries.

goods.name: Fireworks
goods.note: Realgar burns white, verdigris with sal ammoniac burns blue.

goods.name: Spectacles
goods.note: Two lenses in a horn frame. Doubles the working life of every scholar and needleworker.

goods.name: Clocks
goods.note: Brass clockwork behind glass. The Ware that teaches a town to keep hours.

goods.name: Home automaton
goods.note: A golem's clockwork cousin: no blood, no soil, little wit.

goods.name: Obsidian ware
goods.note: Blades and black mirrors.

goods.name: Perfume
goods.note: Scent carried in spirit of wine. Flowers for the first impression, amber for what lingers.

goods.name: Incense
goods.note: Resin on a glowing coal. Every temple needs it every day, which makes it the steadiest luxury trade there is.

goods.name: Lost-wax brasses
goods.note: Model it in beeswax, coat it in clay, melt the wax out and pour brass in. Every cast is unique because the mould is destroyed.

goods.name: Tools
goods.note: Steel edges on wooden handles. Every other workshop waits on these.

goods.name: Muskets
goods.note: Steel barrel, wooden stock, brass fittings. Useless without powder and shot.

goods.name: Cannon
goods.note: Cast bronze, because bronze bulges before it bursts. Iron ones are cheaper and kill their crews.

goods.name: Blasting charge
goods.note: Powder packed to break rock. Mining goes from inches to yards a day.

goods.name: Wildfire
goods.note: Sticks, burns on water, and lime makes it light itself.

goods.name: Reflecting telescope
goods.note: A polished metal mirror instead of a lens, so no coloured fringes. The astronomer's instrument.
